subject: Using native data between different rmr versions

messages.author: 7e01961f1f4ce874
messages.subject: Using native data between different rmr versions
parts:
Hey Antonio,

We run an algorithm which uses previous runs data, which is stored in native format. We are using rmr version 3.1.0 currently and simultaneously trying out 3.1.1.

What I observed here is that I was not able to read data written using rmr version 3.1.0  in rmr version 3.1.1 and vice versa. I have not gone through release notes of 3.1.1. I am not sure if anybody else faced this problem, but if this is the case what would you suggest to overcome this situation while upgrading rmr ?

Should we always write historical data which goes back in our algo in non native format?

Thanks 
Abhishek

messages.author: 6ac7e7dfbe4f6c38
messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#1553] Using native data between different rmr versions
parts:
On Wed, Jul 16, 2014 at 2:45 AM, Abhishek Gayakwad <a.gay...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hey Antonio,

We run an algorithm which uses previous runs data, which is stored in native format. We are using rmr version 3.1.0 currently and simultaneously trying out 3.1.1.

What I observed here is that I was not able to read data written using rmr version 3.1.0  in rmr version 3.1.1 and vice versa. I have not gone through release notes of 3.1.1. I am not sure if anybody else faced this problem, but if this is the case what would you suggest to overcome this situation while upgrading rmr ?

This was certainly the case between 2.x and 3.x and there was plenty of warning about it, but between 3.1.0 and 3.1.1? That's obviously not expected in a bugfix release. I took a look at the diffs and I think I may have introduced an incompatibility while adding support for logical NAs. Logical was mapped to bool in C++  and that meant logical NAs would turn to true or false, I can't remember. So I had to change the representation to take more space, and that breaks compatibility. On one hand, my bad, I could have thought of that. On the other, I think that's part  of the stabilization of the new native format in 3.x. Hopefully that's unique event in the 3.x series. Finally,  there are no tests of format compatibility across versions, and where there is no test there is no safety (it's called "test harness" for a reason). It's not obvious how to write one without embedding test data in the package (so far tests are self-contained in that they generate their own data). If somebody submitted such a test I would certainly look into adding it to the next release. If you or your organization rely on storing data in native format, I would recommend doing that.  Wait, there is another point. A not-so-fun workaround could be to take logical data in 3.1.0, convert it to integer in 3.1.0 and then read it with 3.1.1 and convert it back. If that works my analysis would be confirmed.
Should we always write historical data which goes back in our algo in non native format?

Yes, for long term storage and archival the native format doesn't look like a great option, because of the rate at which changes have been happening and the fact that it is not "standard" in any sense of the term: there is a single tool reading and writing it after all. As far as breaking backward compatibility, it has happened twice (not counting the unwanted latest issue) but this is the first time we don't offer the ability to read the old format by selecting an appropriate format (that is, format change wouldn't be transparent but the fix would be trivial). We looked into it and the added complexity in the code was too much, so we went for a break with proper warning. I think there are two ways forward: 1) pick an archival grade format and offer support for it in rmr 2) Put more emphasis on native adding tests of backward compatibility

I prefer 1) because were one to switch to a different language or what not, having to convert all your data is sometimes impossible and because no matter what we do with the native format, since it has to work within the limitations of the the typedbytes definition (HADOOP-1722) it is unlikely to become a good archival format. But there is the inconvenience of having to switch format whenever writing long-lived data. 


Antonio


 

Thanks 
Abhishek

messages.author: 7e01961f1f4ce874
messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#1553] Using native data between different rmr versions
parts:
Hey Antonio, thanks for quick reply as always.

We have written unit testcases (using testthat) to test RMR in local mode and our test data is in native format. In some dev boxes testcases were failing because of higher RMR version. Thats how we figured out this issue. I don't have any idea as of now to test compatibility issues without having test data, will surely let you know I figure out way to achieve this.

As of now keeping final/reusable output/data in some standard format and intermediate data in native format looks the way to go.

- Abhishek
